target.title: fix(realtime): filter malformed provider tool names
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A malformed or unreadable custom tool name could make OpenAI Realtime, Azure Realtime, or Google Live reject the entire session payload. A shared name rule is also unsafe because the providers accept different identifier shapes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Validate names at each provider-owned payload boundary instead of the shared Talk resolver.
- Preserve every provider-specific valid name: Google permits dots, colons, and a leading underscore; OpenAI permits a leading digit; Azure additionally documents a 64-character maximum.
- Build plain provider declarations after reading the tool fields, so proxies or throwing getters cannot poison payload construction.
- Omit only malformed declarations and log an aggregate count without reflecting rejected names.

No config, command, dependency, or public plugin API surface changes.

## User Impact

Realtime voice sessions continue to start when one custom tool has bad metadata, while valid tools remain available under the exact contract of the selected provider.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox: 87 focused Google/OpenAI provider tests passed after rebasing over the OpenAI greeting state machine: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28753980681
- Exact changed-surface gate passed after conflict resolution: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28754030925
- Exact-head hosted CI passed at `2b88ae691516d21ca1609889f352a93a09058ff8`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28755042646
- Live OpenAI Realtime client-secret probes accepted `1_lookup` and a 65-character alphanumeric name, and rejected colon and slash.
- Live Google Live probes accepted `_lookup` and `calendar.lookup:next`, and rejected a leading digit, slash, and a 129-character name.
- Direct `@google/genai` source and official OpenAI/Microsoft contracts were inspected, including the [Azure OpenAI REST function-name limit](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/reference).
- Fresh autoreview found no actionable issues after the rebase; confidence 0.96.

Known proof gap: no Azure credential was available for a live request. The Azure-only 64-character cap is covered by current official Microsoft documentation and a focused regression.

Release-note context and contributor credit are preserved here; the thanked changelog bullet is queued with the final batch to avoid active-main ordering races.
